paragraphs: On Monday morning, the speaker in the classroom made a small sound. All the children looked up. "Good morning, children," said Teacher Kim. "This is a message for all the children." Lily listened with Mia and Leo.

"Next Saturday, the nineteenth of September, we clean our school field. We start at eight o'clock, and we work for three hours. The field has a lot of old paper and plastic on it. Please meet at the school gate at eight o'clock. Bring a bottle of water and a pair of gloves. We have a bin for paper and a bin for plastic. Coach Matt has more bins and big bags for us. Look everywhere: under the trees, near the school wall, and next to the pond. Do not work alone, and stay with a friend.

"Children from other classes can come, too. Take a note home today, and bring it back on Thursday. If it rains on Saturday, we do not clean the field. Is there anything else? Yes, wear old shoes and a hat. At eleven o'clock, every child gets a cold drink. Thank you, and see you on Saturday!"

After the message, Mia asked, "What else do we need?" "Old shoes, a hat, and a friend," said Lily. "I am your friend," said Leo. "I will carry the plastic bags." "Three hours is a long time," said Mia. "We are many, so it is easy," said Lily. "I like a clean field, because I play football there at lunch," said Mia. Mia looked out of the window and pointed at the field. "Where is the bin by the gate?" she asked. "I can see it from here," said Leo.
Lily wrote it in her book. "Saturday, the nineteenth of September, eight o'clock, the school gate." Then she put a pair of gloves in her bag.
